No. 69       PORT MORESBY, THURSDAY, 21st AUGUST      1975


                      PRICES ORDER No. 146

               A PRICES ORDER relating to the maximum retail price
for
                    MANUFACTURED CIGARETTES
MADE by a Deputy Price Controller under the provisions of the Prices
Regulation Act 1949, as amended to date, to
  come into operation on the date of publication in the Government
Gazette.
1. REVOCATION.
  Prices Order No. 143 is hereby revoked.
2. DEFINITIONS.
  In this Order—
   "cigarettes" means cigarettes which are manufactured in Papua New
Guinea from imported or locally grown
      tobacco leaf.
   "retail" means for the purpose of consumption or use.
3. MAXIMUM RETAIL PRICE.
   (a) The maximum price per packet at which cigarettes may be sold
by retail at any of the locations specified
      in Schedule 1 is the amount specified in the Second Column of
Schedule 2 in relation to the brand and
      pack specified opposite in the First Column of Schedule 2.
   (b) The maximum price per packet at which cigarettes may be sold
by retail at locations other than those
      specified in Schedule 1 is the amount specified in the Third
Column of Schedule 2 in relation to the
      brand and pack specified opposite in the First Column of
Schedule 2.
4. DISPLAY OF PRICES.
  A person or organisation who has in his custody or under his
control any of the cigarettes to which this Order
applies for sale by retail, or who, offers, exhibits or exposes any
of those cigarettes for sale by retail, shall display a
ticket, label, placard or notice attached to or exhibited or
displayed with the cigarettes setting forth in a prominent
position in clear and legible figures easily discernible to any
person inspecting such cigarettes, the price at which
the cigarettes concerned may be bought.

5. MAXIMUM RETAIL PRICE OF CIGARETTES IN CERTAIN AREAS.
  Notwithstanding anything in this Order, where a nctice in writing
is given by the Controller to a supplier of
cigarettes fixing the maximum price at which cigarettes may be
supplied by him in any locality, being a price not less
than fixed by Clause 3 of this Order, the maximum price at which
cigarettes may be so supplied is the price fixed in
that Notice.

    Statute Law Revision (Ministers' Powers) Act 1975.
    Ministers' (Delegation) Act 1975.
THIS legislation affects the exercise of powers and functions by
Ministers. Where a Minister considers it desir-
  able that a person should be authorised to exercise one of his
powers and functions, the Minister may authorise
that person in one of the following ways:—
    (a) where the Minister has been given a statutory power of
delegation—by a formal instrument of
      delegation or subdelegation; or
    (b) where the Minister has not been given a statutory power of
delegation and the person to be authorised
      is an officer in a Department, branch, division or Office for
which the Minister is responsible — by an
      informal authorization (which may incidentally be embodied in
a departmental circular and be given
      by reference to office).
   For the time being the following Ministers have been given a
statutory power of delegation:—
    (a) all Ministers (in relation to entering into and executing
any Government contract or agreement).
    (b) the Minister for Transport and Civil Aviation (in relation
to the Civil Aviation (Interim Arrangements)
      Act 1973).
    (c) the Minister for Defence, Foreign Relations and Trade (in
relation to the Defence Act 1974.)
    (d) the Ministers responsible for the powers and functions
conferred by the Defence (Visiting Forces) Act
      1975).
    (e) the Minister for Education (in relation to any power or
function conferred on him by any law relating
      to education).
    (f) the Minister for Finance (in relation to the Electricity
Supply (Administration Power Stations) Act
      1970, the Port Moresby Water Supply Act, 1941 (Papua), the
Post and Telegraph (Finance) Act,
      1970 and the Stamp Duties Act, 1952).

The above powers of delegation also relate' to regulations and
certain other instruments made under the
specified Acts.
   The statutory powers of delegation referred to may be varied or
revoked by a regulation under the Ministers'
(Delegation) Act. Similarly other Ministers may be given a power of
delegation in relation to one or more
statutory powers or functions by the making of a regulation under
the Ministers' (Delegation) Act.
   Where a Minister has a power for delegation in relation to a
particular statutory power or function no person
(apart from the Minister) may exercise or perform that power or
function unless authorized by a formal instru-
ment of delegation. In relation to contracts and other transactions
with the Government the following classes of
persons are deemed to be delegates:—
    (a) financial delegates (up to the limit of the amount for which
they may approve requisitions):
    (b) procurement officers (up to the limit of the approved
requisition).

                        PRICES ORDER No. 149
A PRICES ORDER relating to the maximum retail price for—

                    PETROL, DISTILLATE AND LIGHTING
                             KEROSENE
   MADE by the Deputy Price Controller under the provisions of the
Prices Regulation Act 1949, as amended to
date, to come into operation on the date of publication in the
Government Gazette.

 1. CITATION.
   This Order may be cited as Prices Order No. 149.

2. REVOCATION.
   The Prices Orders specified in Schedule 2 of this Order are
revoked.
3. DEFINITIONS.
   In this Order—
    "petrol" includes any substance normally sold as petrol whether
or not containing additives of any kind;
    "distillate" includes any substance normally sold as automotive
distillate whether or not containing additives
       of any kind;
    "kerosene" includes any substance normally sold as kerosene
being a medium refined petroleum product as
       used for lighting and cooking in home appliances, whether or
not containing additives of any kind;
    "wholesaler" in relation to petrol, distillate or lighting
kerosene means a person or a firm who sells petrol,
       distillate or lighting kerosene for the purpose of resale and
not for the purpose of use;

    "supplier" in relation to petrol, distillate or lighting
kerosene, means a person or a firm who sells petrol,
       distillate or lighting kerosene for the purpose of use;

       "retail" means for the purpose of consumption or use.

4. MAXIMUM PRICE.

   (i) Subject to Sub-Clause (II) of this Clause, where petrol,
distillate or lighting kerosene is supplied—
    (a) at a locality specified in the first Column of Schedule 1 to
this Order; or

    (b) at some other place at which the petrol, distillate or
lighting kerosene is transported from any such local-
       ity by or on behalf of a wholesaler or supplier;
the maximum price per gallon at which the petrol, distillate or
lighting kerosene may be supplied is the sum of—

    (c) the maximum retail selling price specified in the Second,
Third or Fourth Column as the case may be, of
       Schedule 1 in relation to the locality concerned; and

    (d) the amount (if any) charged for the transport referred to in
paragraph (b) of this Sub-Clause.
   (ii) Where the maximum price of any quantity of petrol,
distillate or lighting kerosene supplied at any one
time, calculated in accordance with Sub-Clause (i) of this Clause is
an amount involving a fraction of a toes, the sup-
plier may charge to the next whole toea.

5. SUPPLY TO GOVERNMENT ETC.
   Nothing in this Order applies to or relates to the supply of
petrol, distillate or lighting kerosene to the Gov-
ernment, Australia or a Statutory Authority of the Government or
Australia.

6. DISPLAY OF PRICES.
   A person or an organisation engaged in selling petrol, distillate
or lighting kerosene by retail shall display in each
of the places of business in prominent positions and in large, clear
and legible figures the maximum prices at which
such petrol, distillate or lighting kerosene may be bought.

No. 74      PORT MORESBY, FRIDAY, 5th SEPTEMBER     1975

Liquor (Licensing) Act 1963, as amended to date

          PROHIBITION AND RESTRICTION OF SUPPLY OF LIQUOR
I THOMAS KINGSTON CIUTCHLEY, High Commissioner, by virtue of the
powers conferred by Section 124 of
 /the Liquor (Licensing) Act 1963, as amended to date, and all other
powers me enabling, and having received
the advice of the Executive Council, hereby—
   (a) prohibit the supply of liquor by each holder of a dealer's
licence, storekeeper's licence and bottieshop
      licence, other than the supply of liquor by the holder of a
storekeeper's licence in respect of a Duty
      Free Shop, for the period 7th September, 1975 to 17th
September, 1975 (inclusive); and
   (b) prohibit the supply of liquor by each holder of a booth
licence, dinner permit, supper permit or special
      permit for the period 13th September, 1975 to 17th September,
1975 (inclusive); and
   (c) prohibit the supply of liquor by each holder of an occasional
licence, unless that holder has the prior
      written approval of the Chief Licensing Commissioner, for the
period of 13th September, 1975 to 17th
      September, 1975 (inclusive); and
   (d) prohibit the supply of liquor by each holder of a publican's
licence, tavern licence, canteen licence or
      club licence—
      (1) on 15th September, 1975, except between the hours of-
        12 noon and 2 p,m. (inclusive) and 4 p.m. and 6 p.m.
(inclusive); and
      (ii) on 16th September, 1975, except between the hours of-
        12 noon and 2 p.m. (inclusive) and 5 p.m. and 7 p.m.
(inclusive); and
      (iii) on 17th September, 1975, except between the hours of-
        12 noon and 2 p.m. (indusive) and 4 p.m. and 6 p.m.
(inclusive); and
   (e) notwithstanding anything in this notice each holder of a
publican's licence, limited hotel licence or res-
      idential dub licence may sell, supply and dispose of liquor on
licensed premises at any time to lodgers and
      their bona-fide guests within any guest lounge on the licensed
premises and lodgers room by waiter
      service; and
   (1)notwithstanding anything in this notice each holder of a
publican's licence, restaurant licence or limited
      hotel licence may sell, supply and dispose of liquor for
consumption in the dining room of the licensed
      premises to persons having a meal between the hours of 12 noon
and 2.30 p.m. (inclusive) and 6 p.m.
      and 10 p.m. (inclusive); and
   (g) prohibit the supply of liquor by each holder of a cabaret
permit for the period 13th September, 1975
      to 17th September, 1975 (indusive).
  Dated this twenty-ninth day of August, One thousand nine hundred

and seventy-five.
                                             T. K. CRITCHLEY,
                                              High Commissioner.

                        Liquor (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1973,
as amended to date

                                   DECLARATION OF PUBLIC PLACES
TT THOMAS KINGSTON CRITCHLEY, High Commissioner, by virtue of the
powers conferred by Section 9 of the
   Liquor (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1973, as amended to date,
and all other powers me enabling, hereby
declare all public places in Papua New Guinea to be public places to
which the provisions of Section 9 of that Act
apply, other than premises which are the subject of a licence or
permit, under the Liquor (Licensing) Act 1963, as
amended to date, for the period of 13th September, 1975 to 17th
September, 1975 (inclusive).

and seventy-five.

             cipation, to the extent determined to be practical and
appropriate; and
           (3) Train Papua New Guineans for all levels of employment
under a specific programme

legislation, agree to involve to the maxi-
             mum extent practicable, Papua New Guinean employees in

           (5) Encourage and assist Papua New Guinean corporate
entities or entrepreneurs in establish-

                           Insurance Act 1974

POLICY GUIDELINES UNDER SECTION 25
THE following guidelines within which the Commissioner shall operate
in the exercise and performance of his
  powers and functions under Part 111 of the Insurance Act 1974, as
in force from time to time, have been laid
down by the High Commissioner in Council:—


Papua New Guinea Gazette    3            No. 77-13th September, 1975

                        PRELIMINARY
1.—DEFINITIONS.
  For the purposes of these guidelines—
    "the Act" means the Insurance Act 1974, as in force from time to
time;
    "the applicant corporation" means a corporation that applies to
the Commissioner for a licence to carry on
      general insurance business under the Act.
                  QUALIFICATIONS FOR INSURERS
2.—FINANCIAL REQUIREMENTS.
  2.1. An application corporation shall be a public corporation.
  2.2. The minimum amount of shareholders' funds held by an
applicant corporation shall be K100,000.00.
  2.3. In addition to the deposit lodged under Section 26(1) of the
Act, the applicant corporation shall have
situated in Papua New Guinea, assets in excess of—
    (a) K100,000.00; or
    (b) 10 per centum of net premium income during the previous
financial year, whichever is the greater.
  2.4. The applicant corporation shall have assets in excess of
liabilities of K100,000.00 or 10 per centum of net
premium income in the previous year whichever is the greater.
3.—CALCULATION OF LIABILITIES AND ASSETS.
  3.1. For the purposes of paragraph 2.4, liabilities—
    (a) exclude-
      (i) shareholders' funds; and
      (ii) liabilities in respect of shareholders' funds; and
    (b) include contingent liabilities.
  3.2. For the purposes of paragraph 2.4 assets exclude in tangible
assets, including expenses of the applicant
corporation in relation to the formation, extension or purchase of
its business or the purchase of goodwill.
4.—INFORMATION MAY BE REQUIRED.
  The Commissioner may require the applicant corporation to provide
information with respect to—
    (a) the value of an asset of that corporation; and
    (b) any other matter that the Commissioner considers necessary.
5.—ARRANGEMENTS FOR RE-INSURANCE.
  The applicant corporation shall make arrangements approved by the
Commissioner for re-insurance of liabilities
in respect of risks against which persons are, or are to be, insured
in the course of its general insurance business.
6.—ADMINISTRATION OF APPLICANT CORPORATION.
  The conduct of the business of an insurer shall he controlled by a

person experienced in general insurance busi-
ness.
                  QUALIFICATIONS FOR BROKERS
7.—BROKERS.
  The Commissioner may require a broker when making his application
for a licence to provide information
that—
    (a) he is a person of good fame and character; and
    (b) he is experienced and competent to carry on the business of
a broker; and
    (c) he has a suitable financial record; and
    (d) he is covered by a professional indemnity policy of
insurance to a cover of not less than 1(75,000.00.
              QUALIFICATIONS FOR INSURERS AND BROKERS
8.—TRAINING PROGRAMME, ETC.
  8.1.—Training of Personnel.
  Every licensed insurer and broker shall make arrangements approved
by the Commissioner for a programme of
employment and training of Papua New Guinean personnel in the
industry.
  8.2.—Utilization of Locally Owned Services,
  Every licensed insurer and broker shall, where available—
    (a) utilize insurance and other facilities of Papua New Guinea;
and
    (b) give preference to Papua New Guinean owned facilities.
9.—NOTIFICATION OF AGREEMENTS INVOLVING FOREIGN EXCHANGE.
  9.1. Every licensed insurer and broker shall provide the
Commissioner with particulars concerning—
    (a) an existing agreement; and
    (b) a proposed agreement,
in relation to Papua New Guinea business, involving foreign exchange
to which he is a party.
  9.2. A licensed insurer or broker shall not enter into an
agreement under Section 9.1(b) unless the prior
approval in writing of the Commissioner has been obtained.
  Dated the twenty-seventh day of August, One thousand nine hundred
and seventy-five.

                                                           WARRANT


                                                 REMISSION OF SENTENCE


To: The Commissioner of Corrective Institution, and


To: Each Officer in Charge of each Corrective Institution specified
in Column t of the Schedule.


WHEREAS each offender specified in Column 2 of the Schedule
committed an offence against a law of Papua New

     Guinea and was duly convicted and sentenced under a law of
Papua New Guinea by a Court exercising crim-

inal jurisdiction in Papua New Guinea:


     AND WHEREAS each of those offenders was sentenced to a period
of imprisonment of 12 months or more

and, but for the grant of this remission, would be due for release
on or before 31st December, 1975;


     AND WHEREAS on 16th September, 1975 Papua New Guinea will
celebrate and achieve its Independence and

the Government of Papua New Guinea and I desire to commemorate this
occasion by partially remitting the unexpired

portion of the sentence of each of those offenders which remains
unserved on and from 15th September, 1975:


     Now THEREFORE. I, THOMAS KINGSTON CRITCHLEY, High Commissioner,

by virtue of the powers conferred

by Section 73 of the Papua New Guinea Aa 1949-1974 of Australia and
all other powers me enabling, hereby

grant to each of those offenders a remission for so much of the
unexpired sentence of imprisonment as remains

unserved on 15th September, 1975.
